title: What's the true cost of a heat pump?
summary: Climate reporter explains heat pumps' emissions savings and finances: fast payback when replacing oil, small savings versus gas, and cold-climate models that work in Maine.

assertions.quote: it doesn't actually make heat -- it moves it.
switching to a heat pump can save you anywhere from about 1 metric ton to about 7 metric tons of carbon emissions every single year.
the prices for a gas furnace are about the same, $10,500 and $6,000
a new air-source heat pump that will fit into existing ducts
electricity is a lot cheaper than fuel oil and don't forget about heat pumps monster efficiency.

verdicts.note: At typical US prices heat from a heat pump costs well below heat from oil, propane or resistance.

assertions.quote: if your home is heated by pretty much anything that's not natural gas, you can expect to save between $800 to $1,200 a year

verdicts.note: NREL and other modelling find the largest bill savings for homes switching from oil, propane or resistance, and the smallest for gas.

assertions.quote: That means that in less than five years your heat pump will have actually paid for itself

verdicts.note: When an oil furnace needs replacing anyway, the incremental cost often pays back in about five to ten years, depending on oil prices and climate.
Fuel-oil homes switching to a heat pump usually take a private economic loss over 15 years at 7%; adoption above 20% is unlikely in cold climates on cost alone.
Most oil-heated homes have positive unsubsidized NPV over 16 years with the minimum-efficiency unit, but that is lifetime value, not a payback within a few years.
At 2017 prices RMI finds electrification costs about the same as heating oil over 15 years (cheaper only than propane), which is not a payback within a few years.

assertions.quote: That means that you'll still be saving some money, just not quite as much.
your heat pump will also double as an A/C

verdicts.note: A heat pump provides both heating and cooling, so it replaces a separate AC, though some homes keep a backup furnace.

assertions.quote: air-source heat pumps that work when the outside temperature is down to negative 31 degrees Fahrenheit.
That state now sells more heat pumps per capita than even the heat pump crazy Scandinavian countries.
Each house, installer, and climate zone means something a little bit different for heat pumps.

verdicts.note: Modelled paybacks range from a few years to never depending on the fuel replaced, local prices, climate and whether the AC also needed replacing.
